html:
Jean-Jacques Dessalines was the general who completed the Haitian Revolution and declared the independence of Haiti in 1804. Born into slavery around 1758, he became Toussaint Louverture's chief lieutenant.

After Toussaint's capture he led the war that drove out the French at the Battle of Vertieres. In 1804 he ordered the massacre of most of the remaining French, and he crowned himself Emperor Jacques I.

He forced former slaves back to work on plantations to keep the economy alive, and his rule angered both workers and the mixed race elite. He was ambushed and killed near Port-au-Prince in 1806. Haitians now honour him as the founding father, and the national anthem is named after him.
